Resolves #21720

You can now drag a card from the very end of a long, windowed board column into another column. Before this change, dragging the last card of a sliced column scrolled to its end moved the body's scroll offset. The window slid back, and the reprojection unmounted the card the drag held. The column entry then waited for an update that never came: the card never entered the target, the drop committed nothing, and the drag proxy stayed on screen. Now `Column#selectWindow` keeps the held record inside the window, moving it only as far as it must, and the window follows the scroll again once the drag ends, whether it drops or not.

Evidence: L3 (Playwright unit + e2e, headless Chromium) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-3); AC-2 is the blocked example's spec. Residual: AC-2, Residual-Owner: #21627.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `SortZone.spec.mjs` "a card held at the end of a sliced column stays rendered when the window moves back". On dev's `Column.mjs` it fails at "the held card stays in its column's body". The real-browser entry and drop are in Test Evidence below. |
| AC-2 | Outside this PR: #21627's example spec drags the last card of its 6,200-card column once this merges. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the board unit family and `test/playwright/e2e/board/`. Local runs on the head rebased onto `5fa8c5561b`: unit 176/176, e2e 33/33, component 1/1. |

## Deltas from ticket

- The window also lets go. Holding the card inside the window had moved `windowStart` away from the body's scroll offset. After the drop, New stood blank above a single card until the next scroll, because the viewport showed its spacer. `Column#windowPinned` marks a held window, and the first projection after the drag takes its start from the last scroll sample again (`9ff2bfe51d`).
- A cancel, an off-board release or a drop where the card already sits writes nothing, so no projection followed it. `SortZone#processDragEnd` now re-projects a start column whose window the held card pinned (`3f8888547d`). The unit arm asserts the window after `onDragCancel` alone.
- The unit arm proves the eviction and not the entry: in the unit environment, the mocked update cycle doesn't settle a column entry after a reprojection. That half is proven in a real browser below.

## Test Evidence

I drove #21627's example (10,000 tickets, New at 6,200) in headless Chromium at 1440 × 900. New was scrolled to its end, and I dragged its last card, `t-6200`, into Triage. I read the drag zone in the App Worker mid-drag:

| | dev | head |
|---|---|---|
| held card | unmounted, `parentId: null` | mounted in New's body |
| New's window | starts at 6081, ends at `t-6191` | starts at 6090, ends at `t-6200` |
| `isEnteringColumn` | stuck `true` | `false`, active column Triage |
| after release | proxy on screen, headers 6200 · 1500 | proxy gone, headers 6199 · 1501, New full of cards |

On dev, mid-column drags at scroll offsets 0, 3,000 and 60,000 px commit, and only the end of the column fails.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] #21627's PR rebases onto this, and its e2e spec drags the last card of New into Triage.

## Commits

- `d086f6231e`: the held card stays in its window
- `9ff2bfe51d`: the window returns to its scroll position after the drop
- `3f8888547d`: and after a drag that writes nothing (from review)

Related: #20874 · prerequisite of #21627

Post-merge validation: #21743 (Resolves #21627) is rebased onto this merge, `2d5d1eb7bc`. Its `BigData.spec.mjs` drags the last card of New into Triage, and the drop commits: the headers read 6199 and 1501, the DOM stays at 550, and New has no blank stretch. 8/8 locally.

The same drive found one remaining engine defect around this code. After the drop, New's viewport sits about one window (110 cards) above the end where the drag started. Measured in headless Chromium at 1440 × 900: `scrollTop` went from 576458, its max, to 566225, which is about the restored window start × the 93 px stride. New is filled, so the spec's emptiness check passes, but it is filled at the wrong place. I own the follow-up as a new ticket, starting with a spec that pins the end position and fails today.
